ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the food web shown, how are reef sharks categorized?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture shows a food web. At the bottom there are green producers, such as phytoplankton and algae; in the middle there are sea-whip, parrotfish, turtles, marine invertebrates, etc.; the red labels at the top include reef sharks, snappers, and groupers. reef sharks are located at a higher position in the food web, and there are arrows from organisms at lower levels pointing to reef sharks. Reasoning: The arrows in the food web indicate that energy flows from the organisms being eaten to the consumers. reef sharks eat consumers at lower levels, so they belong to secondary consumers.
